Practised representing square and triangular numbers with dot pictures.
Ishita drew a 6-dot triangle as rows of 1, 2, and 3 dots.
Ishita explained that recounting a shared corner would double-count it, so it is subtracted.
Ishita identified 3 rows of 4 as a rectangle, not a square.
Ishita represented 10 as triangular rows of 1, 2, 3, and 4 dots; teach-back was not passed.
end.parentNote: Ishita practised drawing dot pictures for square and triangular numbers and explaining why a picture shows a pattern. They clearly explained the shared-corner double-counting idea and corrected the shape mix-up by identifying 3 rows of 4 as a rectangle, not a square. At home, ask Ishita to draw the first four triangular numbers and label each row.
